Temperature: 39.2°C; Pulse: 116 bpm, regular; Blood pressure: 142/87 mmHg; Respiratory rate: 27 breaths/min. Marked pallor and mild digital clubbing are observed. On chest inspection, reduced movement is noted on the right upper thorax. Palpation reveals decreased tactile fremitus over the right upper and middle lung fields. Percussion reveals dullness over the right upper lobe, especially at the apex and anterior segments. Auscultation: markedly decreased breath sounds over the right upper lobe with scattered crackles, coarse crepitations in both upper zones, localized bronchial breathing, and few areas of amphoric breathing. Occasional localized expiratory wheeze in right upper zone. No peripheral edema. No lymphadenopathy detected.
examination_results.Imaging Tests: Chest X-ray: Extensive consolidation and cavitation in the right upper lobe, with large areas of dense opacity and multiple thick-walled cavities (largest cavity measuring 4.5 x 3.2 cm); patchy infiltrates in the left upper lobe; volume loss and retraction of the right hilum. Bilateral fibrotic streaks and parenchymal nodularity suggest chronic changes. Chest CT scan: Destruction of right upper lobe architecture with territories of caseous necrosis, air-fluid levels within cavities, and tree-in-bud pattern seen in both upper lobes. No evidence of pleural effusion, but pleural thickening is noted along the right apex. Tracheobronchial irregularity with narrowing in segmental bronchi on right side.
examination_results.Etiological Examination: Early morning sputum sample: Acid-fast bacilli detected (Ziehl-Neelsen stain, positive, 4+); quantitative culture shows >10^7 CFU/ml Mycobacterium species. Sputum nucleic acid amplification test: positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex DNA with a cycle threshold (Ct) of 18.3. Drug sensitivity testing reveals resistance to isoniazid and rifampin (high-level resistance); sensitive to ethambutol and streptomycin. No acid-fast bacilli detected in urine.
examination_results.Immunological Examination: Tuberculin skin test (PPD, Mantoux): Induration of 25 mm at 48 hours. Interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA, Quantiferon): Positive, IFN-γ concentration 8.6 IU/ml (normal <0.35 IU/ml).

examination_results.Endoscopic Examination: Flexible bronchoscopy: Inflamed, hyperemic mucosa with marked narrowing and ulceration of the right upper lobe bronchus; large, irregular necrotic cavity visualized through bronchial wall defect. Bronchial washing: Ziehl-Neelsen stain positive for acid-fast bacilli (3+/field); nucleic acid amplification test positive for Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex. Histopathology from bronchial biopsy: granulomatous inflammation with central caseous necrosis, Langhans-type giant cells; acid-fast bacilli seen on special staining.
